At the risk of sounding like a rant, I'll like to begin with saying that there were a few elements in this game that I found attractive - especially with playing the first game by Square.  Now the beginning of this sequel had a lot of promise with it's cinematic feel and it's very realistic atmosphere - you feel like you're getting dragged into the game and caring for it's characters.  Unfortunately, this honeymoon period ends rather quickly with a very uninspired cover-shooter with a lack of fresh mechanics.  In trying to maintain realism, the game lacks any actual boss battles but this just means the gameplay is dampered by repeatedly shooting waves upon waves of generic enemies.  The camera becomes a problem in this thirdperson shooter - especially on cover mechanics where it won't shift over the left shoulder correctly at times and putting your avatar smack in the middle of the screen.  The hollywood-esque shaky camera is used often even when you begin sprinting which doesn't heighten the experience or make the action more frantic, it's just a cheap trick that invokes dizziness/confusion.
Now the main focus of this game is the story - unfortunately it's like a hollowed out action movie's plot where it begins with some buildup then quickly deteriorates into "NOOOOOOOOOOO" territory.  The villians become one-offs that should just be dispatched like the hundreds of other faceless mooks rushing at you. The inbetween level voiceovers lose their charm after a few levels and 12 chapters later the game just abruptly ends with a credit screen into a return to the main menu and no actual closure.
The game had the high production values (for it's time) and the potential to be much bigger but unfortunately it falls short in my book and I couldn't recommend it to others unless they were real fans of the first game and wanted to see a continuation.
10/10 would quack again

This is a 2D artistic game in which you literally roll through the evolution of drawn/written communication; there are some simplistic puzzles in teh game and you collect pages to read as well as characters.
One can choose to read the historical blurbs one picks up that is in each backdrop, or just play through the game and enjoy the background whilst not reading a thing (the reading/learning is optional).
I am not the type of person that would go out and buy a game like this (in no way do you need to be a gamer, simply rolling and jumping)... Now that I have played it and have a better grasp about what it is, I say it is deifnitly worth picking up if you can get it for ~$1, albiet I am a cheap (sales) gamer, so it might be worth more to oneself.
If you do see it for one doller and that is nto cheap enough for you, but you know you'll buy more games on steam... it has trading cards so you can always pawn those off to recoup some of your money.
Whilst the mechanics are simplistic and the gameplay is relatively speaking short, if you go on the metric a buck and hour for entertainment, it definitly surpasses it. I liekd to read the pages though... if you really wanted to you probably could finish the game far faster (maybe an hour or less).
ITo recap, this is a game that is worth playing for it is unique, artistic, and you might learn something... and is definitly a game I could see being played in elementary schools to utilize as a teaching tool.

This game only exists for two reasons: the first is to increase your game count and the second is to increase your achievement count on your profile page. You get 1 achievement every 1 second you spend actually playing the game, so you just need to play the game for 5,000 seconds (roughly 84 minutes) and you'll get 100%.
But wait, you read that right. You have to actually play the game... if you can even call this a game. First of all, the main menu is poorly-made. If any, the main menu is a hint as to how the entire game's graphics is going to be, which is essentially a bunch of random Unity assets thrown together haphazardly and then presented as a "game". There's literally no animation in the game. You only face one enemy and they appear to be either giant purple bats or evil spaceships. The sprite just comes flying at you like a kamikaze bomb and that is literally their only attack. Then your character, looks like some astronaut with a gun. You basically hop around the map and shoot those purple things. That is basically the entire purpose of the game.
They have some mundane upgrade system that allows you upgrade your character stats like health, speed, fire rate and damage. Upgrading speed is broken. Too high levels and every time you press an arrow key, your character zips across the platforms uncontrollably and you will most possibly end up dying. Upgrading fire rate is pointless. It doesn't do anything. Upgrading damage is pointless when you reach over 100 damage. The enemies always spawn at 100 health and upgrading your damage beyond that value is henceforth pointless. So, upgrading health seems to be the best option. If you manage to play the game long enough and upgrade health too many times, the value becomes negative and you basically just committed suicide. But wait, there's even more flaws. When you open the upgrade screen, your game doesn't pause. It keeps going. So good luck trying to add points while dodging suicidal purple sprites and shooting back at them. I'm sure it will be fun.
Overall, the whole game is borderline unplayable. The basic functions work, yes, but playing this game will be so painful you would rather put a cactus in your pants, seriously. And yea, about the achievements. Great news for you. You need to be actively playing the game to get the achievements. Pausing the game, going to main menu, alt-tabbing, etc will not give you any achievements whatsoever. And since the achievements are kinda buggy, you may have to spend more than 84 minutes to get 100% since it doesn't always trigger every second. So good luck with that.

I've had my fair share of The Binding of Isaac and what I can say for certain is that this easily falls in my favourite games list. At first when you get into the game nothing really makes much sense, items, goals, levels, story - it's all pretty confusing. But after 2-3 hours of playing and after a bit (20-ish) restarts you'll see that everything is well executed with infinte replayability in mind.
Items are the most helpful and most weird aspect of the game, maybe the only thing that can compare to their weirdness is the story. Every item has its own effect on Isaac's stats and his visual appearance. I can guarantee that at the end Isaac will never look human. Items are randomly generated, like the levels, and add tons of variety and make sure that every run you do you'll get a different experience.
The story is something that most people will probably ignore, or will not notice at all, but it is there. The end game cutscenes are the key component and after a few replays you'll get what it's all about and will probably want to find out more, to which I say that you should pick up the DLC for the game. It finishes the story and fills in some missing parts.
The DLC is awesome, since it adds even more variety to the game, but be warned that if you're new to The Binding of Isaac and if you haven't put in a bit over 10 hours don't buy it just yet, because it makes the game a lot harder and might leave you struggling at the starting floors again. But aside from that all the new items and the new trinket system involved really help the game feel even more genuine and diverse.
In conclusion, I'd just like to state again that the game is awesome and well worth the money. It's a good option to have when you want a fun and new experience and only have an hour to spare. When you get into the game it's gonna be hard to put it down. So why wait, start your experience now!

**Binding of Isaac**
Story (6/10):
BoI's story is simple; a boy is stranded in the basement of his home, chased by his abusive Mother who believes it is God's will that her son must die. In all honesty, the story is not very important to the game, and is not a focal point.
Gameplay (8/10):
BoI plays like a standard 4-directional shooter, introducing a gameplay style that is easy to learn, but difficult to master, so to speak. The game introduces numerous enemies, and staggering amounts of upgrades and items that the player must use to utilize throughout the game. Combined with an unforgivingly hard difficulty, the average player should be prepared to die. A lot. Unfortunately, the game sometimes is hindered by its forcing of the player to only shoot in the cardinal directions, since enemies come from all sides.
The game's ability to randomize the levels/powerups through each playthrough gives you motivation to continue to play, and feels satisfying throughout.
Visuals (8/10):
The game has a cartoony, Flash presentation, similar to Super Meat Boy, that is pleasing to the eye. McMullen paints a dark picture of Isaac's basement, introducing horrible creatures and disturbing imagery that is not always as cutesy as the main character. The game is obviously not trying to be a graphical powerhouse, and it works.
Sound (7/10):
Solid, suspenseful music, combined with apt sound effects, give me no complaints about this aspect of the game.
Replayability (10/10):
BoI's entire purpose is to be replayed, over and over again. Games are very short, either because the player dies from the game's brutality, or finishes the playthrough (only takes an hour or so). Usually, a playthrough will unlock new items, reveal new strategies for the player to use, or provide some other incentive for the player to try again. The game tries to be addicting, and succeeds immensely. It's hard to put this game down once you pick it up.
OVERALL:
BoI is successful in what it tries to do; make a rogue-like arcade shooter with RPG elements that allows for many quick plays, that incentivize the player to keep going. It's a real treat to play.

First off, I didnt pay for this game. I got it for free with my now Motherboard. Also this review is from the first 6 hours of gameplay.
First hour and a half, Amazing. I loved it, the intro felt like i was playing a movie. Was beautiful and well writen.
I am a huge fan of Mafia II and was dissapointed they removed a lot of the mechanics from it. Such as not being able to buy your own food, getting pulled over and fined for speeding, chaning your licence plates (As far as i can tell so far you can not do up your cars at all)
The whole race thing could have been a whole lot better. Drive past a cop? a blue marker comes up. Thats it. Thats pretty much as far as that goes. Racial profiling would have been great if it was in more depth. Getting randomy stoped in the street, or pulled over for no reason. Making you feel more on edge and tense. Making you feel really discriminated. But i never really felt that.
Another thing i noticed is that yes, this is a story about a guy that builds his own mob from the ground up. But it does not feel like it. In mafia II. You were no one, you were kissing asses and going deeds just to get someone to notice you to build up your mob career, but in this from the start even when you own no terf, it still feels like you are in control. I never felt like i was nothing, or outnumbered. Playing on hard with no aim-assist I still always felt like i had the upper hand even with no back up and only using a pistol.
Saying all this, it is still a really good game. Graphics? Beautiful. Sound track? Amazing! Story? So far I am enjoying it and intrested as to what else unfolds. Though they took a LOT out that i enjoyed from Mafia II the story is intresting enough and the mechanics it still does have are enjoyable enough for me to want to continue playing.
In its current state, i would say if you enjoy open world mob games. Go for it! personally. For £35 i feel you are going to get your moneys worth. If its on sale for less. Grab it! Its a bargin!

There are two kinds of bad games that exist in the wild: Those that know that they are bad, and those that are bad and try fruitlessly to be good. Guess which one Warmode is? First off: Warmode is about as generic of a shooter as you can get, it features the bland, old formula of Terrorists VS. Counter-Terrorists that we’ve seen a million times now. It features a generic cast of weapons from M4’s to P90’s snipers, shotguns, etc. etc. You’d be forgiven in thinking that this game doesn’t sound all THAT bad, I mean come on, it’s just sounds like some generic shooter dreamt up by some Call of Duty fanboy who payed a moderate amount attention in his 11th grade computer science class to learn the basics of coding enough to get a copy of Insert Generic Game Engine Here to make a first person shooter, but the real meat of this game is in its mechanics, or lack of. This game has about THE most broken mechanics I have ever seen in a shooter, and I’m not talking about “Promised game-changing mechanics are clucky and gimmicky”, no. I’m talking about the fundamental parts of what makes modern FPS games tick are broken and glitch. All guns for some strange reason the same accuracy spread, you can iron sight while reloading, this doesn’t even matter, because iron sighting doesn’t help much regardless, the KNIFE has accuracy, so you basically have to be standing still in order to knife someone, sometimes you randomly die without any mention of who killed you, or how you died, and that’s just scratching the surface of how broken this game is. The maps are too small to have any meaningful firefight, with the exception of one map, two of the maps are still in block out with placeholder textures spewed everywhere, the spawn protection gives no indication of when it where’s off, leading you to empty full magazines into the opponent, only for him to notice your presence and promptly take you out like he’s God or something, and on occasion, you are flung into the air like you’ve been scooped up by a magical, invisible, tornado, only to return to the ground unharmed (Because of course this game doesn’t have fall damage). Overall, you’re better off making your own shooter than to play this peace of crap excuse for a multiplayer game.

As of writing, I've only played 2.2 hours of this game.
They're probably the best 2.2 hours I've ever spent on a game in my entire life.  Not just for an early access title, but even compared to a full release.  Sure, there are things that could be added; but so far, everything's really polished and thought out.
This game plays very well.  It's unique; it has game mechanics that I haven't seen before.  It feels balanced, but it's not forgiving: one or two shots will, at medium or close range, completely obliterate someone.  And that's the beauty of it: the game's is deliberately action-focused and fast-paced: no extra fluff required.  Saying that, all the aspects of this game just click - the graphics, the soundtrack, the gameplay, the map design... everything.  For an early access title, this is one of the best games I've played so far.  It's not competitive, it's not huge - it's a fun game that anyone can play regardless of skill.
It's easy to learn; difficult to master.  I can already tell that the learning curve in this game is steep and I'm looking forward to it :)  I highly recommend this game!

The controls will likely frustrate you.  Straight up frustrate you.  At first it's no big deal, and seems rather simple in the first levels.  Sort of ho hum even.  Then it gets a little harder toward the last few levels and I kept complaining about the controls.  After some time I realized it was not *really* the controls.  It's the fact that it's a rolling object.  Certain physics come into play such as driving a car in a GTA game - it's sorta hard to control things.  You have to take acceleration and corners into account quite a lot.  By the last levels you are not really playing the level so much as fighting the controls and practicing them over and over.  It's got a forgiving checkpoint system, but it seriously sucks the fun out of the game when you realize the levels are only testing how well you can adapt to the wonky controls of a rolling object.  Art is awesome, visually stunning yes.  Informational as well.  I learned quite a bit about typography.  But, I usually prefer my games to have challenging levels with tight controls and this may be the opposite for a lot of people.  I begrudingly give it a thumbs up, only because I wanted to enjoy the game more instead of being frustrated.  I can't in all honesty give it a thumbs down because I enjoyed the style, art, and concept which is a good chunk of why I play games in the first place.  The LOL level nearly made me rage quit, I'll say that much.

Imagine a first person shooter that tells you exactly how much damage you do when you hit something, so you can know for sure the server registered your hit and how well it did.  Now imagine this system isn't accurate in the slightest, and oftentimes your damage is higher than a specific enemy has health, and it still doesn't die.  For example, emptying an entire clip into an enemy standing still, dealing damage equal to more than double its health, then dying a short time later only for the server to tell you "16% of your shots hit" during the last life.
Throw in some latency compensation that favors people with higher pings, usually causing anyone with a 300ms or higher ping to top scoreboards.  Combine that with frequent updates that "rebalance" the game, often completely nerfing one aspect of the game and overpowering another, never really reaching any equilibrium.  Finally toss in that as the game updates, it will oftentimes completely butcher its own files, causing you to have to reinstall or manually edit the configuration to get it to work again without crashing/booting you from any server you attempt to connect to.  With all this in mind, you get all that is good about Natural Selection 2.  On top of that, there don't seem to be many people playing it these days anyway.

One of the greatest games ever.  Playing Hotline Miami is like a nostalgic fever dream.  One of my top ten games ever, I cannot recommend it enough (as long as you can stomach the gore and violence, don't worry it's 16-bit-ish).
Although this game is sort of old news now (the sequel has been out for a while), if you haven't played it, get it now.  And I suggest you stick to the classic way of playing it, on PC, keyboard and mouse.  It has since its original release been ported to nearly every console that can support it but play it on PC.  If you use a controller you do not have the freedom of moving the cursor everywhere unless you hold a certain button.  If you use mouse you'll have the freedom and precision you'll need and of course you'll have a view of the room if you hold shift.
I'll confess I know very little idea as to what the story is.  You play a guy who's always wearing a high school jacket and an animal mask (different masks give you various powerups).  You go around the levels and just kill anyone in your way.  It is intentionally done in a classic style, one that brings to mind the days of going to the local Blockbuster and bringing pizza home to have a family dinner + movie night.  The asthetic and gameplay are just mint.
Even better is the soundtrack.  This game introduced me to what is now my favorite music genre, synthwave.  If you are unfamiliar, synthwave is basically 80's styled music.  There are different subgenres such as pop synthwave, dark synthwave and even vaporwave is a branch of synthwave.  I used to have the soundtrack of this game on my phone and I listened to it all the time, commuting to and from work.  I have since upgraded my music stereo to a cassette player.
The gameplay, the nostalgia, the graphics, the music, the sheer mindless fun of playing a videogame is all here.  I cannot recommend Hotline Miami enough.
Update:  Apparently the main character's name is officially known as Jacket.

I went into Life is Strange (hereafter LiS) looking for a decent substitute to the tried and true Telltale Games formula for interactive storytelling. Little did I know that it would end up winning me over with its combination of charm, clever gimmicks, and the heartfelt portrayal of its characters.
There are two great strengths on display here. The first is its believable depiction of a town called Arcadia Bay: a place that's just as quaint as it is rough around the edges. Framed by a moody and oftentimes sublime indie soundtrack, this is a small town that's coated in a sunny and carefree facade that gradually flakes away as the story bothers at it. There's a real personality to this place where beauty and rust have come to mingle.
The second, and perhaps greater triumph of LiS, is its earnest approach to characterization. Don't misunderstand me here, I'm not saying every storyline or conversation comes off as masterful. There's some unfortunate dialogue issues in the phrasing department and not all characters have satisfying arcs to their development. But there is something just so refreshing about how earnest this story is. Some of the characters really grew on me despite my initial dislike for the lot of them. I was delighted by the many layers of complexity that the story allowed for the people that live in this snow globe. Just about all of the cast, be they major or side characters, gets a chance to surprise you with a depth you might not expect.
It would have been so easy, so simple for this story to slide into jaded cynicism as it approached the finishing line but that's not the last impression Arcadia Bay leaves you with. Long after I had completed the game I found myself still puzzling over the little town and its many inhabitants. There's a sort of pervasive air of mystery that holds on even after the game is over and it leaves you curious as to what other secrets are still be waiting to be told.
As to some of the shortcomings of the game: it is an uneven experience overall. Some of the episodes are head and shoulders above the rest, with the last two episodes feeling rushed and a tad bit sloppy. The graphics are serviceable but dated and the facial expressions can be very hit-or-miss. That's understandable given when it was released, however. You can expect the story to drag a bit as it continues to swap between simulating the life of a female photography student in high school and the overarching narrative of getting a handle on your dominion over the march of time itself.
Speaking of which, being able to rewind conversations and pick another outcome if you don't like the aftermath is a novel way of making sure you get the result you want. Being able to learn the outcome of a dialogue option before committing takes the guesswork out of where the options in conversation will leave you. Choose carefully! Delicious twists and turns abound as you plumb ever deeper into the beating heart of Arcadia Bay.
My recommendation is that you give this game a chance. I didn't have high hopes for this one but I came to love it despite some flaws. Come for the earnest characterization and stay for the pathos.

Before I start this review let me just remind that is just my opinion if you believe something I say is not true then that is your opinion write your own review. I will also not be comparing this to any other previous Mafia games, the reason for that is because this game stands no chance compared to other Mafia games. The previous Mafia games had such a compelling story, while this one is mediocre at best. So instead I will recognize this game as is own and ignore its unfortunate tittle. I will also try to refrain from spoiling too much.
Story   RATING: 3 / 5
Mafia 3 has a very weak story in the long run. In the beginning of the game the story is pretty good but after that it just becomes a normal revenge story. You get thrown in the game knowing nothing about Lincoln Clay other than the fact that he is a Veteran and he was an Orphan at a young age (Which is only found out by Dialogue, no cutscenes or gameplay.).  After the Introduction act, they give you half of the missions to do and the other half after the first half then you’re done. These “missions” are all basically the same expect for the “boss” of that mission. While the story is pretty weak the storytelling is really good. Mafia 3’s story is told like a documentary; you play in the past while every time you complete a part of a “mission” you get an interesting cutscene of the future in a form of an interview talking about your choices (there is not many to make). But that’s really the only form of story you get other than the ending and beginning. There is other parts but they aren’t that significant.
Gameplay RATING: 3.9/5
The gameplay is probably the only reason I kept playing this game before I realized that most of it was optional. Mafia 3 has a Stealth system which is extremely easy to manipulate. So, easy in fact you can go into a warehouse full of enemies and take them all out, without anyone even noticing. You can stand right in front of them and it would take them about 3 seconds to still realize your there and another 2 just to start yelling and shooting, but in that time, you could have already killed 5 people with Stealth takedowns. Mafia 3 also has another takedown system but this is louder? Well it really isn’t, let’s say someone does see you well you’re in luck just use a Brutal takedown and no one even noticed. Brutal takedowns are so easy to do, if you didn’t like taking your time and being stealthy just do brutal takedowns no one stands a chance against them.  The guns are game are nothing special, If you use a mouse then it’s a pain just to aim (they slightly fixed it since launched) but they shooting is pretty fluent nothing special. Driving in this game is the same it works good and at times it can be fun. But the gameplay overall gets repetitive fast. Other than stupid fetch side quests there nothing to do in this game but the story.
Customization RATING 1/5
Every Open-World game should have customization, right? Nope, not here, Mafia 3 has nothing of the sort to customize your character or car (other than 2 car upgrades you get later) and it sucks. There were times where I got bored and just wanted to mess with my character and car but I could not do that and it really bothered me. I don’t care if it’s going to come in DLC it should have been in the standalone game.  There are a couple of game settings you can change but not a lot, but at least we got some.
Is it fun to complete?
Absolutely not, completing this game to 100% was such a chore. I had to play through the 3 game times to get different endings and kill the bosses different, and it wouldn’t be so bad if didn’t have to sit through the dialogue scenes what are annoyingly long. But there is no reward for it either, there not even an achievement for collecting on collectibles. What’s with that?
TL:DR
This game is mediocre at best and if you want to something to pass the time then go ahead and buy this game but do it when it’s on a sale. But if you want rich gameplay and rich story then save your money any buy something like Witcher 3 GOTY (which is like 100x better).

5/10

8/10

This game has fast-paced play and brings some interesting ideas to the FPS genre. You don't reload you weapon, you "harvest" a new one from the plants that grow up where the bullets that have been shot hit the ground! There are several types of weapons in addition to the corn-based shotgun, such as a "Peastol" pistol, and asparagus-based sniper rife, and the powerful "Carrocket Launcher" which will blow your opponents away... if you can hit them. There are also melee weapons: a standard-issue shovel, and an axe. The controls and weapons feel great, and the game's art is quite fun. Several game modes and maps add good variety to the gameplay. Since this is an early access title, and the game is still being worked on, you can expect more content to be released and bug fixes to be steady, but the game is already a winner in its current state. I highly recommend giving this game a go, even if you've never played an FPS before.

Hotline Miami Review
One of the greatest games ever.  Playing Hotline Miami is like a nostalgic fever dream.  One of my top ten games ever, I cannot recommend it enough (as long as you can stomach the gore and violence, don't worry it's 16-bit-ish).
Although this game is sort of old news now (the sequel has been out for a while), if you haven't played it, get it now.  And I suggest you stick to the classic way of playing it, on PC, keyboard and mouse.  It has since its original release been ported to nearly every console that can support it but play it on PC.  If you use a controller you do not have the freedom of moving the cursor everywhere unless you hold a certain button.  If you use mouse you'll have the freedom and precision you'll need and of course you'll have a view of the room if you hold shift.
I'll confess I know very little idea as to what the story is.  You play a guy who's always wearing a high school jacket and an animal mask (different masks give you various powerups).  You go around the levels and just kill anyone in your way.  It is intentionally done in a classic style, one that brings to mind the days of going to the local Blockbuster and bringing pizza home to have a family dinner + movie night.  The asthetic and gameplay are just mint.
Even better is the soundtrack.  This game introduced me to what is now my favorite music genre, synthwave.  If you are unfamiliar, synthwave is basically 80's styled music.  There are different subgenres such as pop synthwave, dark synthwave and even vaporwave is a branch of synthwave.  I used to have the soundtrack of this game on my phone and I listened to it all the time, commuting to and from work.  I have since upgraded my music stereo to a cassette player.
The gameplay, the nostalgia, the graphics, the music, the sheer mindless fun of playing a videogame is all here.  I cannot recommend Hotline Miami enough.
Update:  Apparently the main character's name is officially known as Jacket.

Brainy Joy:
~~~~~~~~

As everyone knows by now, I really enjoy puzzle games; anything from casual to the most challenging ones, such as MYST. If you enjoy this type of game like me, and on top of that get a buzz out of killing demons, then you might like to have a go at Brainy Joy.
Brainy Joy is a casual game where you have to eliminate all the demons within each level to unlock the next one.
Brainy Joy is quite easy to understand, but if you need some assistance, feel free to press on the help button and you’ll find a good run down of the game. Essentially, all the levels are nodes and roads that link each other together. In some of the nodes, you might have enemies (demons), scrolls, medical packs and wands. Each of your enemies will have a colour attributed to them and a certain number of points to eliminate them. There are four types of demons: blue, green, purple and red. You’ll need two points to kill the blue demons, four for the greens, eight for the purples and sixteen for the reds. The interesting point is that you will start each level with a melee weapon which will only give you eight points in hand. The trick is to find the right path to collect the right items to kill the demons. For example, the green coloured scroll will eliminate the green demon and your character will avoid being damaged. If you don’t have a scroll, you’ll have to use your melee weapon but the enemy will be able to retaliate and you’ll lose health points. Bear in mind that the maximum number of health points your character will ever have is eight. Don’t try to use your melee weapon on an enemy who has eight points worth of health. Don’t despair, there are other alternatives: if there are wands or scrolls on some of the nodes, try to find a way to reach them. Wands are particularly good to use on foe as they will save you half of the point to eliminate a demon. For example, purple demons need eight points to eliminate but if you have four points available on your wand, you’ll kill the demon and avoid any attack from him. The scroll works pretty much the same way. The green scroll will eliminate one green demon, for example. Also, in later levels you will be pursued by a sorcerer to make it slightly more difficult.
In regards to the graphics, they are mediocre in my opinion, but they suit the gameplay very well. The soundtrack is fun and it is easy to play. One aspect I personally don’t like is the fact I can’t play on a full screen.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Nice and easy to play
-	Nice soundtrack
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Graphics need to be polished
-	A bit repetitive
-	No achievements or trading cards
Brainy Joy is a nice casual puzzle game.

This was slighty enjoyable. The puzzle aspect to it is not too terrible, but it does need some work. For example, you have a healthbar in red and a mana bar in blue. This isn't normally bad, but the problem is that it shows no hp. It shows that you will have this much health under the swords icon or in other words how much you can hit them for HP when you use your own to attack. This is a little bad as no enemy ever has their attack stated outright, but it's usually how much hp they have remaining. For example, the blue jester can do 2 hp of damage. It can also do 1 if it doesn't have as much hp. You can only tell this from clicking on them and then engaging in a fight. Luckily, you can use the redo option to make sure you don't mess up too badly. The biggest problem I might have with this is the puzzles though. The early stages seem fine enough, but it feels as though there are multiple solutions. If this is intended, then it's fine, but if it isn't, then it's a problem. Because of your HP, you can only attack an enemy up to 6 of your max 8 hp. Any damage that equals or is over 8 will kill your character. The health kits help, but the problem is that you can stack some of them and waste their potentials. They give you 4 HP or 4 attacking points. Anymore than 1 at a time will waste about 2 to 4 x the medical kits used after the first one. It's not all bad as the graphics do the job well enough to consider not being too harsh on the eyes, but they are very lacklusters, I feel as though I've already seen these sprites as well as the sound used at the end of each level. I'd say it's a good brainteaser and a good timewaster, but I wouldn't recommend too much as its gameplay does turn kind of stale once you realize that the only changes to the environment are usually only higher enemies to fight or different items to pick up with the occasional arrow only allowing you to go up or down/left or right in a direction, but never the other. The last is kind of negated by the fact that the early levels only really show you what's to come ahead, but I wasn't really invested in it as I do other puzzle games.
Pros:
-Graphics are fine and do their job, but leave much to be desired as they look very lackluster compared to other games of the genre. It works for their intended purposes, yet don't be expecting much.
-Gameplay is good, but it's repetitive and really boring. The most you might do is solve the puzzle easily, but because of the early levels having multiple solutions from what I can tell, it just feels okay to finish a level.
-Soundtrack is really decent. There are multiple tracks and they all work along with the sound effects. My biggest issues with those however comes from the fact that some don't really fit the tone. For example, one of the early levels has a dungeon-like or tension-like music in the background and it didn't seem fitting at all at least to me. For what looks like a very kid-friendly game, it's weird to hear music that might make the kids a bit startled at least.
Cons:
-No achievements or trading cards. This isn't really a fault on the developer's, it's just something they don't have. I won't deduct any points for it, but people looking for a game about those will need something else to satisfy their desires.
-Not engaging. I'm sorry, but I just can't seem to get into the swing of things. Even with the music on, it just felt downright boring to do stuff. I'm not sure what causes it, but it might be the fact that the gameplay isn't as easily investing as other puzzles might be. For example, in a game like Portal where there's a story with the puzzles and as you complete more puzzles, you get more of the story.
Overall Rating: 4/10 or a 5/10 is what I would rate this game. It ain't downright terrible, but it could be a lot better.
Comments: For a puzzle game, it does its part of the job right, but the other stuff is very...difficult to really get a true hang on it. Without playing the game for yourself, you might expect that if you used magic, you would get hit. This isn't true in this game, but it feels weird that as far as I can tell no tutorial is present so the only way to know the controls is either to read the help or just play the game. Oddly enough, I found many grammatical mistakes which is bad because some english speakers could be turned off by this. For example, in the wizard section, not counting stuff like commas or parentheses, there exists at least two different spelling errors. Easely is supposed to spelled easily and then hey are frozen is missing the t part of the word they. I would recommend a proof-reading of the readable documents/other stats from an english speaker as they might be able to help out more than others assuming the developer's english isn't their native language.

Before I start this review let me just remind that is just my opinion if you believe something I say is not true then that is your opinion write your own review. I will also not be comparing this to any other previous Mafia games, the reason for that is because this game stands no chance compared to other Mafia games. The previous Mafia games had such a compelling story, while this one is mediocre at best. So instead I will recognize this game as is own and ignore its unfortunate tittle. I will also try to refrain from spoiling too much.
Story   RATING: 3 / 5
Mafia 3 has a very weak story in the long run. In the beginning of the game the story is pretty good but after that it just becomes a normal revenge story. You get thrown in the game knowing nothing about Lincoln Clay other than the fact that he is a Veteran and he was an Orphan at a young age (Which is only found out by Dialogue, no cutscenes or gameplay.).  After the Introduction act, they give you half of the missions to do and the other half after the first half then you’re done. These “missions” are all basically the same expect for the “boss” of that mission. While the story is pretty weak the storytelling is really good. Mafia 3’s story is told like a documentary; you play in the past while every time you complete a part of a “mission” you get an interesting cutscene of the future in a form of an interview talking about your choices (there is not many to make). But that’s really the only form of story you get other than the ending and beginning. There is other parts but they aren’t that significant.
Gameplay RATING: 3.9/5
The gameplay is probably the only reason I kept playing this game before I realized that most of it was optional. Mafia 3 has a Stealth system which is extremely easy to manipulate. So, easy in fact you can go into a warehouse full of enemies and take them all out, without anyone even noticing. You can stand right in front of them and it would take them about 3 seconds to still realize your there and another 2 just to start yelling and shooting, but in that time, you could have already killed 5 people with Stealth takedowns. Mafia 3 also has another takedown system but this is louder? Well it really isn’t, let’s say someone does see you well you’re in luck just use a Brutal takedown and no one even noticed. Brutal takedowns are so easy to do, if you didn’t like taking your time and being stealthy just do brutal takedowns no one stands a chance against them.  The guns are game are nothing special, If you use a mouse then it’s a pain just to aim (they slightly fixed it since launched) but they shooting is pretty fluent nothing special. Driving in this game is the same it works good and at times it can be fun. But the gameplay overall gets repetitive fast. Other than stupid fetch side quests there nothing to do in this game but the story.
Customization RATING 1/5
Every Open-World game should have customization, right? Nope, not here, Mafia 3 has nothing of the sort to customize your character or car (other than 2 car upgrades you get later) and it sucks. There were times where I got bored and just wanted to mess with my character and car but I could not do that and it really bothered me. I don’t care if it’s going to come in DLC it should have been in the standalone game.  There are a couple of game settings you can change but not a lot, but at least we got some.
Is it fun to complete?
Absolutely not, completing this game to 100% was such a chore. I had to play through the 3 game times to get different endings and kill the bosses different, and it wouldn’t be so bad if didn’t have to sit through the dialogue scenes what are annoyingly long. But there is no reward for it either, there not even an achievement for collecting on collectibles. What’s with that?
TL:DR
This game is mediocre at best and if you want to something to pass the time then go ahead and buy this game but do it when it’s on a sale. But if you want rich gameplay and rich story then save your money any buy something like Witcher 3 GOTY (which is like 100x better).

Let's start by saying that I played it without any previous knowledge of the game, and without using any guide, walkthrough or that sort of things. So if you tackle it in the same manner, you are in for a 45 minutes game.
Now, let's talk about the game.
Visuals
I can say that it looks pretty good, the use of high contrast between two colors was nice to the eyes and it gave the game a interesting feeling. Also, the level design was simplistic and good.
Gameplay
In the gameplay department, you can expect a walking simulator. You are going to walk around and be a little lost at the beginning, but at some point it became pretty straightforward. The puzzles, if i can call them like that, aren't hard at all, they are also the classic example of games puzzles "find an item" and "press some buttons".
Music
At some points it gave momentum to the atmosphere of the game, at some other points it just made me ask myself "why this started to sound out of nowhere and it sounds like this?", so I have mixed feeling about it.
Plot
Being a 45 minutes game don't expect an intrincated and profound plot, not saying that short games can't be like this but just this this particular game. You have interaction between characters, which at times are pretty weird (and this could be good or bad).
Taking into account all this I can say I recommend it, but I don't know if at full price. It's not a "must play before you die" kind of game, but it is definitly worth checking. And just adding to my opinion of the game, I think it could have been so much more.

The sequel to The Moon Sliver, Szymanski's third Steam walking puzzle narrative game is a strong one. Szymanski allows us into this world he's created from The Moon Sliver to help answer questions left in the previous title. Firstly, this game is significantly higher priced than The Moon Sliver, so I have to say, if you didn't care for Moon Sliver, you should pass on this, because it's more of the same at a higher price tag.
If you were like me and LOVED The Moon Sliver, then you would be as eager as I was to play this game. It does answer the questions left in The Moon Sliver while introducing us to some new concepts and characters.
I really don't want to give away ANYTHING to do with this game. Primarily because it IS a short game and I think it's best for the player to learn about everything in real time as they are playing to fully appreciate it. I would even recommend avoiding the "About this Game" if you have managed to do so thus far. What I will say is what you can see by the pictures: the game's stylization is vastly different from either of Szymanski's previous walking puzzle narratives. It may be a little offputting to some who like the more realistic style, but it doesn't detract from the story or gameplay at all. In fact, I think it only adds to it. Going through Szymanski's world could best be described by the Heinlein book "Stranger in a Strange Land." You never have a sense of ease with the game, but your desire to learn more is what presses you on.
"The Music Machine" is worth the price, and a pretty memorable installment in Szymanski's library. Especially when you find out exactly what The Music Machine really is.

Natural Selection 1 is my favorite competitive/cooperative multiplayer shooter of all time. Natural Selection 2 is a fantastic continuation of the franchise. The main draw of the game is that there are two asymmetric teams, the colonial space marines vs. the zerg-like Khara. The space marines have to take locations and fight with the Khara over resource points. Both teams play primarily like most shooters in a first person perspective, however both teams also have a commander who views the map from a top down, RTS-like view.
The commander's job is to give his team orders, build various structures, and plan out strategies against the opposing force. This sounds complicated, and initially it is very difficult to play. Natural Selection 2 has a very dedicated, albeit small community who have been playing this game for a long, long time. Therefore they are often a little dickish to newcomers who come into the game, since the weakest link in a chain can cause them all to fail. However, if you make an active effort to learn the mechanics and strategies required, you'll be having a lot of fun working with your team, either setting up ambushes in dark places as the wall-climbing skulk or burning away alien structures with a flamethrower. The team synergy that is capable in this game is the best in any multiplayer game, but due to the complexity and the steep learning curve most people who try out this game never find it.
It's a shame that Natural Selection 2 has been operating at a bit of a loss for Unknown Worlds, since a bunch of their keys got stolen and sold on illicit websites. This game goes on sale for $2.99 and was in a couple of Humble Bundles, so it should be pretty darn cheap to purchase. Everyone should at least try it out for that price, and who knows, maybe it'll be your new favorite multiplayer game!

Type:Rider is a platform game where you learn about different typography styles while solving the levels and puzzles. Within each level there are three types of collectible;
Letters of the alphabet - These do nothing except make you feel like you've completed the level correctly.
The Ampersand - Essentially the same as the alphabet letters but are more well hidden (usually)
Asterisk's - When you pick these up you unlock a small section of history within the level selection / progress screen. This will give you background on the creation and circumstances surrounding these fonts.
The levels themselves aren't really all that challenging and once you fail or die reiteration of a section is very quick, with exception of the final, hidden, level. That one is just evil, if you die you start at the very beginning (thankfully all the pickups remain 'picked up').
All in all it's not a bad game, if a little brief, I personally wouldn't recommend buying this at full price because it's easily completed within about an hour. But if you can get it for say £2 or there abouts it's worth looking into.
Of course it does help if you have an interest in typography.

would not recommend overall. i'll list my reasons below and you can judge for yourself.
i almost never submit reviews for games i play, but since i found the reviews that i read for this game overwhemingly contradictory to my gameplay experience, i will share my judgment.
(i admit that if you do not value gameplay, and are satisfied with custcenes and storyline/character development you will find the reviews i read of the game to be consistent with your experience playing the game)
i'll list the good things first:
1. plot storyline and characters are good. (side note: voice acting gets strange sometimes, e.g. when you have one character interrupting another, the interruption is way too delayed and feels akin to bad acting) overall voice acting is good though.
2 .cutscenes are good.
3. graphics are good.
the bad things:
1. interacting with objects in game. oh god. you have to be standing in the right spot in order to interact with any simple thing such as a door, a ladder, or even loot. and when i mean the right spot, i mean the spot is sometimes so annoying to find that sometimes you will question if you're even supposed to open that door, climb that ladder, or if there is even loot.
2. the loot. enemies drop loot, that's nice and all, but the problem is that they don't drop it instantly and compounded with the trouble with picking it up makes for a very poor way to gather loot. it's distractingly difficult to pick up items dropped from enemies; that is if you even notice them in the first place.
3. the combat animations. you'll notice the standard messy combat system here and there but what was a gamebreaker for me was when i was wielding a spiked club as a weapon and my attacks would still make the same sword animation, sword sound effects, and sword bloodspray and cuts. what? i couldn't stop laughing for a while, and honestly i considered listing this as a positive lol. just kidding, it sucked.
4. this might have been just me, but the entire game felt like it had a built in 160~250ms delay. i'd move the mouse and it would respond 160ms later, i click W to move forward and my character would move forward 160ms later. i highly doubt it's something wrong with my game and it's noticeable enough for me to be distracting. i hope this isn't a real issue though.
5. minor things. sometimes a patch of nearby ground would flicker black for half a second. no jumping allowed (which sucks in my opinion). progression is lifelessly linear (and i mean accomplishing an objective is basically finding a path from point A to point B, storyline is not perfectly linear).
overall, after about 2 hours of playing this game, everything about it mixed together made me have this strange desire to go take a walk outside in the sun. when i came back i didn't want to open it again

At the risk of rehashing what other people have said, Life is Strange is not a masterpiece of a game. But it IS a masterpiece of an experience. Starting out, I never expected this 5-part episodic adventure to fundamentally change me as a person. But it did. And now I find myself ruefully returning to Chloe's room every so often and just sitting there, reveling in the nostalgic atmosphere. Never have I been so emotionally invested in fictional characters as I was with Max and Chloe and even now, days after finishing the game, they still manage to find a way into my errant thoughts through the day. LiS did a great job at instilling the sensation that when Max was with Chloe, she felt like she belonged. Everywhere else was a cold, unforgiving place - but here, with your friend, you were cared for. Loved. And I think it's that feeling that really got me hooked on Life is Strange as a brilliant character analysis.

I was a great fan of the original and while this plays pretty much the same, the magic is gone for me. Shadow of Mordor and its Nemesis system worked great with a story of revenge. I was emotionally invested and I felt like I really should kill every orc in existance because damn it they killed everything I loved.
Shadow of War tries to one up the original and while it is epic, it just falls flat, becoming maybe a bit too awesome and over the top (and the original already stretched the possibilities of Middle-Earth setting as it was).
The simple (yet beautiful) upgrading of you gear through "forging a legend for your weapons" was replaced with uninspired items that drop of random orcs and so the shattered sword of your dead son you used as a dagger and your tool of revenge is swiftly cast aside for Rohirim dagger #298 you can upgrade usung dull rune system with 3 possible gem types to slot into it.
The ability to dominate orcs is an upgrade to drain ability (which you can use only 1 out of 3 possible) so either you choose this game defining one, or any of the cool ones (while you could've combined these before).
The upgrade to Nemesis system where orcs can attack you and whatnot falls flat when you find intel on one captain who proceeds to ambush you 15 seconds afterward because you were asking questions about him. The fact that some orcs act like you fought them countless times before while I saw them for the first time doesn't help either.
And there are many more little details that are not actually gamebreaking, but did not make sense to me and overall were taking my already low enjoyment out of the game.
Otherwise, I may have even recommended it because it is objectively a solid game even though I did not enjoy it half as I was expecting I will (which is damn shame as I was really looking forward to it). But the lootcrates are the straw that break camel's back here. While it is not in your face and can be comfortably ignored it is there and you can feel they designed the game with it in mind. I would probably not buy it were it another game, but I did because as I said - big fan of the original. While I played it enough to get my money's worth at least, can't say I enjoyed it. Big dissapointment here.

So, everyone looking in these reviews are probably doing it because of the controversy, so please let me addess every point and I will refute them.
Grind- Many say they don't like the grind... But the game is level based. If you enjoy the gameplay the grind shouldn't matter. The missions don't feel repetetive because every single captain is unique, looks different, and plays different. Because of this, the way you play the game will vary based on the weaknesses and strengths the captains have, so every mission is rather interesting because of the twists the captains put on them.
loot boxes- Inconsequential. People who say they don't like them and that they ruin the game... I beat it just fine without the boxes and I would never dream about cheating by getting them. Loot boxes in this game are the easiest thing to beat. All you have to do is not buy them and they will stop coming. There is no reason for you to buy them, no real advantages they give you that you can't earn, so you should just ignore them entirely like I did.
Now that we have covered the two things that I hate in reviews for this game. Let me tell you some of the things that I love about the game.
Leveling system of the captains- Lots of people say they don't like that bosses are trapped to your level... Well OF COURSE THEY ARE!!!! You are their boss, and betrayals are things that can happen in this game. Would you feel like the boss if you are level twenty but you got lucky and branded a legendary level thirty? NO! You would use that one level thirty and just gang♥♥♥♥♥♥every other captain and warcheif with him and beat the game like it was nothing. They fixed this by forcing you to play within your bounds. You can only recruit captains below your level or at your level, they can only level up to your level, and if they are higher you have to shame them when you beat them, and then hunt them down and recruit them to your army when they are at your level. (ALSO- The shame mechanic is ♥♥♥♥ing awesome because is ACUTALLY makes them go more and more insane every time you do it. It is as if you rip a part of their soul out with it and seeing its effects feels so badass. You can basically completely shatter the spirit of a higher leveled character until he is in pieces on his knees.)
captain combat- I LOVE fighting captains. It is always different and some of them can be rather difficult. Some capatains are really weak, and some are absurdely strong. On top of this, some directly counter your upgrade path, and some are perfect for it. In other words, you get an upgrade that lets you burn enemeies, one guy is immune to fire. Well♥♥♥♥♥♥ one of your abilities is now cancelled and you have to find another way to do it. Or maybe they are immune to vaulting so you have to get creative with how you manuever around him. Every boss has different strengths and weaknesses and this forces you to change how you play and change your strategy with EVERY SINGLE one.
Army system and seige- Much like in the first game, you have captains and warcheifs. They added a new enemy at the rank of overlords, they are badasses with tons of perks and abilities. Since everyone is randomly generated some will be a lot more godlike than others. Anyways, when you go into a land, you are faced with an overwhelming number of enemies. About twenty to twenty five captains, a max of five warcheifs, and an overlord. You have to start dwingling on that number of captains until you can gain the ability to seige a castle. For every warcheif on their team left alive or unbranded their defences will get stronger and you will have to fight one of those warcheifs at every objective you come to. So the best strategy is to take them out beforehand so they are either on your side or taken down. Now its seige time, and holy ♥♥♥♥ will it feel badass. You get to pick an eventual max of five captains to join you in your seige and each can be accomponied by upgrades of soldiers, war beasts, animals, seige weapons, and more. So you need to arrange your army so they are balanced. If your captains die, rest assured it will be permanent and it will hurt your seige. Your army and your captains storm a castle and you plow a line through the army while your men follow up behind you until you push through every capture point and face the overlord where you, and you alone, must fight him and his remaining goons before you can kill him and make the castle yours. Fail to kill him, and there will be consequences. He will most likely capture some of your captains and you will have to free them before you can go back and face him.
Riding beasts- Oh my god, if the first game did this well then they killed it with the second one. Riding beasts feels so badass in this game. They have caragors, which die rather quickly to some captains, but they are fast and you gain the ability to use your might (like rage gained by hitting people) to call more friendly caragors in to fight for you. Once you get your numbers going you can lead a small pack of badass oversized dogs to fight and kill for you. Graugs are ♥♥♥♥ing beasts in this game. Just walking will knock over most of your enemies. They are hard to beat, but once you have them oh my god it is rewarding. It just feels badass to crush your opponents with your huge war beast and it gets better with the elemental ones which are harder to kill but can breath ♥♥♥♥ing fire, or ice, or whatever element you capture them in. But, the most badass in the game, the drake. Thats right, you can break and ride a fire breathing ♥♥♥♥ing dragon. I rest my case there.
highly recommend, it is a game that will completely capture your focus for more than thirty hours even if you are one of those people who hates doing missions to gain XP. the fighting never gets dull, the enemies are always interesting, and the missions are diverse as well. If you get this game, you won't be dissapointed.

This is an excellent premise for a game, and I'm extremely disappointed I couldn't reccomend it.  I say this a fan of the two earlier games from David Szymanski - Finger Bones and The Moon Sliver.  What ultimately sank it for me is the buggy save system - the game is supposed to save automatically upon exit (There is no provision to manually save) but on three occaisions I re-started the game to find out that was NOT the case.    The last time was after significant progress was made and I had made it past a particularly unnerving and creepy section of the game had no desire to repeat, not to mention the 30-40 minutes of lead-up time.
The game's aesthetic doesn't really do it for me either.  There are times it looks really great and adds to the other-worldly feel but unfortunately there are a lot of times where the game falls victim to its own gimmick and the monochrome graphics obscure or unnecessarily complicate the viewing environment.
I also take particular issue with one section of the game that
goes completely against the open world exploration aspect.  Its even stated in the load/start menu to "Relax, take your time and explore" which is most assuredly not the way to approach that stage.
The story is very intriguing and dialogue driven and for that I give major points, its just a shame everything couldn't come together in execution.  I'm hoping the next adventure-genre game from David Szymanski improves upon the shortcomings of this one.

I can now confirm that I have a very soft spot somewhere in my heart dedicated to 2D Action RPGs, sometimes known as Metroid-Vanias.  It's not exactly a well-populated list, now that I think about it, but I count among it some of my favorites like Metroid, Megaman, Odin Sphere, and now Dust: An Elysian Tail.
So yeah, that's the short description.  Side-scrolling action RPG.  If it had stopped there, it would have been a wonderful romp down video-game memory lane, but it didn't stop there.  Dust took that basic framework for the gameplay, and then decided to bring so much more!
Beautifully animated and excellently voiced, this game follows the story of a strange animal-person thing that has no memory of its past but somehow has a decent grasp of two languages: english, and turning enemies into red powdered sugar.  The story is engaging enough, and the characters a very well realized, even if one of them has a tendency to get a little on my nerves.  The main strength this game has is  the combat.  The combat is very intuitive and responsive, to the point of being borderline-overpowered in a skilled set of hands, and I had a blast flying around the battlefield, juggling enemies in massive 1,000+ hit combos without ever touching the ground.  I suggest playing on a harder difficulty if you have any experience with fast-based action-RPG's, simply because I felt like nothing could challenge me with even the minimal amount of grinding.  The combat is literally a whirlwind of combos and skill, and once you get a hang of it you will have a blast.
As for a downside, this game has a habit of teasing you with areas you can't reach until much later in the game, though backtracking is common for Metroid-Vanias.  Luckily, that's helped by a dynamic map system that keeps track of all the areas that still house unclaimed treasure.  It never felt grindy, but some areas did take a little longer to return to just to receive a slight boost to my character's money.  The crafting is also a letdown, as it is mostly just a straight upgrade to stats, without offering more options for playstyle.  Still, this downside is less of something that was done wrong and more of something I wanted added, so really, I can't fault the game for that!
All in all, this game was a surprise winner.  I hadn't heard anything about it beforehand, but now it's in the running for my Game of the Year.  This game even has shoutouts to other recent indie games!  It's little touches like that, built upon a solid foundation of sidescrolling action, that let you know that Dust: An Elysian Tail is something special.

A really fun and educational casual platformer, especially for those who have an interest in art/graphic design and history.
You jump around through linear levels, collecting letters of the alphabet and reading material dispersed throughout. And you can read it whenever you feel like, even skip it entirely if you want. It's pretty mellow like that, but I think it's engaging just enough with the challenge factor while still managing to be a pretty relaxing experience. It's a pretty short game if you're just looking to blast through the levels, but I got some extra time and enjoyment out of it by reading all the material as I went along and collecting everything. Finding all the ampersands should prove to be a particular challenge, since there is one per level and they are quite hidden.
I am proud to say that I like this game enough to have gotten every achievement, including that dumb Facebook/Twitter post one. I don't even have Facebook or Twitter, so this sort of achievement is dumb and irritating to me. But hey, I just borrowed my sister's account to get it. I still really like the game, but this sort of thing annoys me. A video game's achievements should never have anyhting to do with external social networking sites. This is nothing significant in terms of the game, but it's something that stuck out for me and I though it was worth mentioning, since I know there are others like me who aren't really into Facebook or Twitter, even if we may seem few and far between. We anti-Facebook people gotta stick together, y'all! We should totally make a Facebook page for our kind.
Anyway, this being a game about ♥♥♥♥ing fonts, it's a very niche sort of game. But I happen to really like font, so this game appeals to me, that very specific sort of person who enjoys graphic design and history and delicious, glorious fonts. Gameplay-wise, it's nothing new or groundbreaking; it's a very simple platformer and there isn't much to it. But, again, if you like art, history, or art history, this is a fun (and educational!) trip. And I commend any game that can be fun AND educational, and also be centered around something as esoteric as fonts.

The Binding of Isaac is a fantastic game. It is ridiculously cheap, continously supported through fantastic (also cheap) DLC, and an upcoming remake on a better platform (the game running on Flash is honestly the biggest negative about it). It's a must-have for anyone who enjoys Rogue-likes, bonus points if you're partial to the Shootmania genre as well. Each playthrough is unique, unlocking random items as you go to power up (or down) your chosen character and procedural creating the dungeon you crawl through, making certain that no two playthroughs are ever the same. The progression in the game is also one of the more natural I have ever experienced. The pool of possible items to pickup widens, more stages unlock, and the enemies get more difficult as you play and win more. I honestly cannot think of a game on Steam that gives you more bang for your buck than The Binding of Isaac.

David’s games may not be for everyone but they have most definitely grabbed my attention.
I started off with The Moon Sliver, looking for a cheap, short and easy walking simulator to pass the time. It’s not often that I play something and have it linger in my mind afterwards with questions and curiosity. I was left quite impressed and I decided to look into the others too.
The Music Machine caught my eye with it’s quite unique graphic style. I’d never seen that in a game you could explore before and I’m quite a sucker for “pretty” games generally.
The games minimalist style may seem bare and shallow, but it was more than made up for in it’s writing and character interaction.
You play as a young girl, whose body has been possessed by a ghost. She’s trapped in a body she can’t control and you explore not only what is going on in the world around you, but what the relationship between the two is all about. I personally quite enjoyed how the characters bantered with each other and although most of the time it seems a love/hate relationship, you soon realise that there is a depth to why her incorporeal friend is there.
The game was short, me weighing in at 3 hours for two playthroughs, but it was definitely worth it in my opinion. If you like chill games and don’t mind the controversial tag of “Walking Simulator” then I would think this is something you might enjoy. Sure, gameplay comes down to walking around, but the story is interesting. If you enjoy philosophy or even psychology, then I think you would be interested.
I have to say, I didn’t expect this to make reference to and expand on the previous game I had played but I was again quite impressed that it did. It was subtle, but it answered questions and intrigued me all the more. I would recommend that you play “The Moon Sliver” first, then come back here if that one grabs you like it did me.
Both great games in my opinion, I look forward to anything else that David puts out there.
TL;DR : Nice unique graphic style, a short game with an intriguing story that is partially linked to it’s predecessor “The Moon Sliver”. A great game if you don’t mind walking simulators with a slight philosophical or psychological interest.

This game has very basic plot, is rather short, but IMHO is very fun. The move upgrade options make fights more visually interesting over time.  But more importantly, I feel that the game mechanics caters to a variety of playing style. For example, to deal with incoming enemy attacks, there are some options:
1. Use "normal" block and dodging/dashing. Requires player to move a lot.
2. Use "Just Guard" block (which can block anything including boss attacks, but requires more precise timing)
3. Use "Flourish" counterattack (which requires even more precise timing but nullifies incoming attack while dealing damage to the attacker at the same time).
As a result, players can opt to run around and attempt strikes here and there whenever opportunity arises (i.e. more button mashing), or alternatively keep their character relatively static and use well-timed blocks/counters to defeat opponents.
The game will be better with more polish in the art/writing/sound department. More level variety will be nice too. Then again, AFAIK this is an indie game made by a small team with limited budget, therefore, I feel that the current shortcomings are understandable. Hopefully the dev team will be able to get more resources for their future projects :)

Enjoyment of Type:Rider will likely hinge on one's interest in, or curiosity about, typography. As a platformer the game is rather standard, though the two dots (colon?) are somewhat unwieldy. Nowhere is this more evident than the in the bonus level, modeled on Comic Sans MS and some of the internet's more hackneyed tropes. The level requires a degree of precision which is hard to gauge from the low level of detail presented by the player avatar. That being said, this mostly isn't an issue, as the game is rather easy as far as platformers go, the puzzle levels are relatively simplistic, and the game is forgiving as well, with frequent checkpoints, making it suitable for more casual platformer players.
As far as integrating the educational material into the gameplay goes, it doesn't. Information about the history of type is present in snippets of text that are picked up in the form of collectables in the levels. Most collectables are rather easy to find, save one that I noticed several Let's Play videos missed. Also "missed" is the particular reason for Comic Sans's failure. As a typesetter once told me, CS was intended to be used at a 6 pt size. Unlike many other typefaces, CS is completely legible here. When made larger, it comes to look ridiculous. While I'm at it, the game misuses the word "font," which actually refers to a particular size, thickness and style of a typeface, not merely the typeface. That being said, I still found it pleasant to take breaks from the action for an illustrated slice of the history of type.
In spite of its shortcomings Type:Rider is a breezy, short game with handsome presentation that should make a nice parfait for afficianados of the printed word.

Spintires Review --- MorrisReview --- 16 July 2015
STORY AND GAMEPLAY
Spintires hasn't got a real story, it's more like a game, where the player can complete many tasks. You play as a russian lumberman and you task is it, to transport logs from one point to another point on the map. You complete your mission with old Russian trucks in a world out of mud, water (rivers and seas) and very big forests, which are distributed on the map. At this moment, Spintires offers you 6 different maps, more of them are in deployment.
The primary intention of Spintires is it, to drive the different old trucks, to find a way completing your mission. You do that in the third person perspective on the left side near your truck. Once started the game you can decide what you want to do:
Explore the world and find new ways to complete your task?
You want to try something out or only playing in the open world?
Or want you to play in the multiplayer?
It's your choice!
TECHNOLOGY
In Spintires you have a lots of options to change the game. Next to the basically options you can play Spintires also with the Gamepad, Xbox 360 controller or a wheel.
The controlling and timing fits well with the game.
The graphics and sounds are fluently also on middle sized computers, but sometimes small lags could you be appear. Graphics a very detailed, for example mud, which flies around you vehicle and realistic water animations. How realistic it is, is addicted to the power of your computer.
The game maybe won't start at the first time and could crash while playing. To save your progress there is only one memory location, if you want to start a new game on another map, you have to delete the old memory unit.
POSITIV's and NEGATIV's
+ beautiful and realistic locations and vehicles
+ detailed trucks and settings
+ also controllable with alternative methods
+ continued deployment
+ two game modes for individual simulation
+ available in 16 languages
- start problems, crashes and save problems
- lags while playing
- "only" six maps and a handful of vehicles
- possibly difficult controls
- Multiplayer is possibly very insecure
CONCLUSION
Spintires is a good game with a great idea and a lots of potential in it. But until it's great or perfect, there is missing a lot of work and time. This game is something for people, who have fun driving big trucks with bigger mileage or who are a bit bored and want to taste a day of work with lumbermen.
Actually Spintires costs 24,99€ on steam, I don't really recommend the game for this price, wait until it's on sale or deployed longer.
Because the game is already under deployment, I will write more reviews with more actual information in the future!

A well-known movie critic once declared that video games can never be art.  He was entitled to his opinion, and I bear him no ill will.  But I wish he could have played a few games like this before he passed away.  Type: Rider feels more like an art experiment than a game.  It's short, it's not particularly difficult (though collecting everything is quite tricky), and the actual gameplay is pretty simple.  This is one of those games you just play for the ambience, and in this case that's a pretty good reason.  This is a must-buy for typography geeks, but still fun for almost anybody.  And yes, the dreaded Comic Sans does show up, but only as a bonus level.

The Binding of Isaac is one of my all-time favourite games. The game is hard to define, but you must battle through dungeons collecting items and defeating bosses. There is no save button and the difficulty is high. It is the kind of game that you could play for hours and have an entirely different experience with each run. That is because the dungeons, bosses and items are all randomly generated. There are also multiple unlockable characters to choose from, all with different stats and effects.
Storywise, this game is minimal. The plot is based on the biblical story 'The Binding of Isaac'.  However, it is good that the plot is minimal, because it works. This game doesn't need a huge plot, character development or plot twists, because its a game you can jump into without needing to know the story. The main fun of this game is the gameplay, which is simply incredible. Dungeons get bigger and bigger with each level, and harder mobs appear after every two floors. The boss battles are amazing, having a wide variety of gimmicks. The controls are perfect. Arrow keys to fire your projectiles, space for you rechargable special item, Q for tarrot cards and E for bombs, with the WASD keys for movement.
The game was made by the same team that developed Super Meat Boy, which is a very good thing, as it seems to share the same morbid art style. The soundtrack in this game is top-notch. The boss battles sound like epic battles, making you feel like a badass. The further you go down, the more depressing the music gets, which suits with the theme of the game.
So overall, this is a highly replayable game. Dungeons are randomly generated, items can change a game for better or for worse, bosses are challenging, controls are great and so much to do. I would highly recommend this game to anyone that wants to buy a good game. The best £3 I ever spent.
Also, if you worried that you won't be able to run it, it only takes up megabytes of space, and it could work on my old crappy laptop, so you should be fine.
